title: Denmark tests humanoid robots in supermarkets to help to ease staff workload at night
key_facts: At a Føtex supermarket near Copenhagen, humanoid robots are being trained to pick up products and place them on shelves.
The robots were developed by Danish start-up Hive Robots and built by China's Unitree; they have been training since June.
For now human operators guide every movement, which helps the AI learn to handle different products.
The ambition is for the robots to restock independently by early 2027, mainly at night when the store is closed.
The test is part of a wider trial with Salling Group, Denmark's largest retailer, with more than 2,000 stores in six European countries.
According to Føtex, staff spend 40 to 50 per cent of their time replenishing shelves; the retailer hopes robots will take on some of this work so employees can help customers.
The robots are slower than people and need close supervision; Danish law would have to change before they could work autonomously among shoppers.
